T1053.name: Scheduled Task/Job
T1053.description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling to execute malicious code at system startup or on a scheduled basis for persistence.

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task
T1053.005.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for malicious code execution.

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
T1059.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

T1059.001.name: PowerShell
T1059.001.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

T1059.003.name: Windows Command Shell
T1059.003.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell (cmd.exe) for execution.

T1059.005.name: Visual Basic
T1059.005.description: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VBS) for execution via wscript/cscript.

T1059.007.name: JavaScript
T1059.007.description: Adversaries may abuse JavaScript for execution via mshta, wscript, or browsers.

T1003.name: OS Credential Dumping
T1003.description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials from the OS to obtain account login information.

T1003.001.name: LSASS Memory
T1003.001.description: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of LSASS.

T1003.002.name: Security Account Manager
T1003.002.description: Adversaries may attempt to extract credential material from the SAM database.

T1003.006.name: DCSync
T1003.006.description: Adversaries may attempt to access credentials via domain replication service (DCSync attack).

T1547.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
T1547.description: Adversaries may configure system settings to automatically execute a program during system boot or logon.

T1547.001.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
T1547.001.description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to a startup folder or referencing it with a Registry run key.

T1218.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
T1218.description: Adversaries may bypass process/signature-based defenses by proxying execution of malicious content with signed binaries.

T1218.005.name: Mshta
T1218.005.description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious .hta files and JavaScript/VBScript.

T1218.010.name: Regsvr32
T1218.010.description: Adversaries may abuse Regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code via COM scriptlets.

T1218.011.name: Rundll32
T1218.011.description: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

T1569.name: System Services
T1569.description: Adversaries may abuse system services or daemons to execute commands or programs.

T1569.002.name: Service Execution
T1569.002.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows service control manager to execute malicious commands or payloads.

T1021.name: Remote Services
T1021.description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a service for remote access.

T1021.002.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.description: Adversaries may use SMB to interact with or move laterally to a remote network share.

T1548.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
T1548.description: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevated privileges to gain higher-level permissions.

T1548.002.name: Bypass User Account Control
T1548.002.description: Adversaries may bypass UAC mechanisms to elevate process privileges on a system.

T1087.name: Account Discovery
T1087.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of accounts on a system or within an environment.

T1016.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
T1016.description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access.

T1069.name: Permission Groups Discovery
T1069.description: Adversaries may attempt to discover group and permission settings.

T1068.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
T1068.description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate privileges.

T1210.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
T1210.description: Adversaries may exploit remote services to gain unauthorized access to internal systems.

T1558.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
T1558.description: Adversaries may attempt to subvert Kerberos authentication for credential access.
